ignore.reason: This rule is JUDGED. It reports every string site inside a unit whose file also calls any helper that two or more files call, and then asks a model whether the helper already produces that value. It never decides the value itself, so this exception is not a claim that the rule is wrong -- it is noise control on a machine with no TYPESAFE_API_KEY, where onUnavailable: 'report' prints every candidate as an unverified warning. All twelve candidates were the English prose of a tool description or of a report line, and no helper in this repository produces either. The exception is scoped to extensions/** so that the rest of the repository is still checked, and it can be deleted on a machine that has a model key. See the feedback note in the README.

Judged, and unjudged here for the same reason as single-path. The candidate is any guard whose test names a field that some declaration types as boolean; RunOutcome.timedOut beside code/durationMs/stdout/stderr and Clamped.truncated beside text are two such candidates. The judge is given the flag's owner declaration and its field list, so it has what it needs to answer 'independent' -- a flag that selects behaviour while no value changes meaning. This exception exists because no key reached the provider, not because the rule cannot tell.

Judged, and unjudged here for the same reason as single-path. The candidate is any string literal of four characters or more, containing a lowercase letter, inside an exported unit that two or more files call; readJson is exported, two files call it, and it contains 'utf8'. The literal filter admits identifiers, encodings and format strings BY DESIGN, because the rule refuses to keep a vocabulary of caller-naming words -- its own docstring records that matching route names was the coupling that had to go. 'utf8' is therefore a true candidate, and only the judgement separates it from a caller's label.

Judged, unjudged here, AND a genuine gap worth reporting. The candidate is any exported function containing a continue; workspace skips a directory key and is exported, so it qualifies. Its caller is a test, and that is the gap: joggle already knows what a test file is -- policy.testFiles holds the pattern and workspace records unit.test -- and check.ts uses it to keep test declarations out of duplicate-implementation. This rule does not consult it. Skipping unit.test here would remove this finding in every repository, not only this one. See the feedback note in the README.

The rule pairs 'this function derives a boolean' with 'some declaration in this file records a boolean' and does not check that they are the same fact. Three findings, none of them a fact recorded twice: scriptsFrom derives looksLikeAnOption(name) while ScriptsConfig records respectGitignore; readIgnoreFile derives 'the line compiled' while IgnoreRule records negated; timeoutMilliseconds derives 'the caller named no timeout' while respectGitignore is recorded again. A subject comparison would settle all three. Reported as feedback; the exception is scoped to this package so the rule still runs on the rest of the repository.

isIgnored skips a rule that cannot apply to the path -- a directory-only rule tested against a file, or a rule declared in a directory the path is not under. Nothing is dropped from a caller's view: the function answers one boolean question, and the rules it stepped over were never going to change that answer. The rule reads a `continue` in an exported function as a funnel that shortened the caller's data. Reported as feedback; see the note in the README.

evidence.repository: A Pi extension: a Node program that runs inside the Pi process and registers one pi tool for every package.json script under the directory pi was launched in. It renders no components and depends on no Effect runtime, so the composition and effect rule families are not enabled here.
